title: Buying and selling horses and ponies using the VAT margin scheme
text:
There is additional information you need to record if you sell second-hand horses and ponies using a margin scheme.

 There is also the British Equestrian Trade Association ( BETA ) form you can use instead of keeping a stock book and invoices.

 When you can use a margin scheme

 Horses and ponies must be second-hand to be eligible for a margin scheme.

 A second-hand horse or pony is one that has previously been owned by somebody else.

 When you cannot use a margin scheme

 You cannot use a margin scheme if:

 • you bred the horse yourself and are selling it for the first time, as it is not classed as second-hand

 • VAT is shown separately on the purchase invoice for a horse or pony you have bought

 Ways to account for VAT

 There are 2 ways you can account for VAT. You must either:

 • keep normal margin scheme records including the specific information set out in the section titled ‘If you use normal margin records’

 • 
 use the BETA form — then you do not need to keep a separate stock book or invoices

 If you use normal margin scheme records

 You must add extra information to your records.

 If the purchase price of the horse or pony is more than £500, you must either:

 • record the unique identifying passport number

 • ask a vet to certify that the horse or pony is the one described on the invoice

 You must also add:

 • colour

 • sex

 • type or breed, for example, cob or thoroughbred

 • age, if known

 • height

 • stable name, if known

 • distinctive markings

 How to work out the margin and VAT due

 You should calculate the margin and VAT due using the normal margin scheme rules .

 Records to keep

 If you do not use the BETA form

 If you do not use the British Equestrian Trading Association form then you should keep normal VAT margin scheme records .

 If you buy and sell at auction and do not use the BETA form

 You should keep the normal margin scheme records. You must include enough information in your stock book to identify the horse or pony, as mentioned above. 

 There are specific rules that apply for auctioneers — read Using the auctioneers VAT margin scheme .

 If you use the BETA form

 The British Equestrian Trading Association form contains all the stock and sales records you need for the margin scheme. If you use this, then you do not need to keep a stock book or invoices.

 Further information

 You must show any goods you buy or sell using a margin scheme on your VAT return .

 If you use an agent

 You should refer to the specific rules for VAT margin schemes that apply for agents .

 Tertiary legislation

 You can find the legal conditions in VAT Tertiary Legislation :

 • Section 2.4 — additional information requirements for horses and ponies

 • Section 2.5 — BETA scheme for horses and ponies
